package.description: Locks your screen for a set amount of time, so you actually take that break.

en-US.author: telcoray
en-US.description: Locks your screen for a set amount of time, so you actually take that break.
en-US.longDescription:
Digital Detox is a small Windows app that locks the screen for a chosen duration, from 1 to 999 minutes.
The lock screen covers every monitor and shows a countdown; common shortcuts such as the Windows key and Alt+Tab are blocked, and the screen switches off gradually.
It unlocks by itself when the time is up, lives in the system tray and can start with Windows.
en-US.name: Digital Detox
en-US.releaseNotes:
New: Digital Detox for Android (preview)
Digital Detox now also comes as an app for Android phones, released together with the Windows app and with the same version number.
- Detox, Pomodoro and Sync, like on Windows
- Pair the phone with your PC using the usual 6-digit code: a detox or a Pomodoro started on one starts on the other too
- While a session is on, other apps are covered. Calls stay reachable, and there's an emergency exit
- No account, no ads, no tracking: sync stays on your local network
It's a first preview for Android 11 or later. To use it, Android asks for the accessibility permission (used only to cover other apps during a session) and for notifications. android/README.md explains why each permission is needed.

Download
- Installer: download DigitalDetox-v2.8.4-setup-x64.exe and run it
- Portable: download DigitalDetox-v2.8.4-win-x64.zip, unzip it and run DigitalDetox.exe. No installation needed
- Android: download DigitalDetox-v2.8.4-android-arm64.apk on your phone and open it. Android asks you to allow installing apps from that source
Since the Windows files aren't code-signed, Windows SmartScreen may warn you the first time: click More info → Run anyway.
